messages:
matt: We just got a sudden flood of OOMs on gpu-serve-prod-17 — ~120 over 3m. Tail latency spiked. Who's oncall?
anya: I'm oncall, joining. Any obvious signal: kernel path, KV expansion, or batch spike?
linh: Perf snapshot shows an abrupt shift: batch sizes doubled for a subset of requests and KV hotset expanded with many long prefixes. Kernel didn't switch; still on the high-workspace path. Workspace-sized allocations jumped from ~900MB -> ~2.1GB for some requests.
kevin: Immediate mitigations I recommend: enable small_batch request_shaper for prod-17, lower allocator.soft_reserve to 0.6 for that pool, and throttle routes that allow seq > 2048. Can apply as quick patches.
tess: +1. Also trigger targeted kvcache eviction on that host to reclaim ephemeral latched prefixes: kvcache.evict(host=prod-17, target_pct=25).
ciara: If we evict aggressively we'll get regeneration pressure. Add a coldstart-rate-limit to 2r/s and set kvcache ttl to very short on ephemeral namespaces.
anya: Applying shaper now. Running: infractl nodes apply --target gpu-serve-prod-17 --patch request_shaper=small_batch
deploy-bot: @anya started run: infractl nodes apply --target gpu-serve-prod-17 --patch request_shaper=small_batch
anya: Shaper applied. Starting kvcache eviction with target 20%.
linh: Pushed a temporary kernel selection override for prod-17: prefer quantized low-workspace kernels for seq > 1024. This reduces workspace allocation on the critical path.
kevin: Also enabling a short circuit policy to route non-SLA traffic off prod-17 for 5m: routing/circuit set --pool prod-17 --policy degrade_non_sla --duration 300
tess: Circuit applied. Watching metrics.
ciara: Set kvcache ttl override: kvcache.set_ttl(pool=prod-17, ttl=30s) for ephemeral prefixes to accelerate eviction.
anya: Live stats: headroom changed from -4% to +18% after shaper + kernel fallback. OOM rate dropped to 4 in last 2m. Latency tail recovering.
matt: Good. Capture recommended near-term persistent settings so we don't hit this again tonight.
linh: Suggested persistent defaults: 1) small_batch shaper for heavy-seq model routes, 2) allocator.soft_reserve=0.6 for pooled GPU nodes, 3) automatic kvcache ttl < 60s for ephemeral prefixes, 4) probe-driven kernel selection that prefers low-workspace/quantized kernels when headroom < 20%.
kevin: I'll open an RFC with config diffs and rollout plan. Also add an alert: gpu.headroom_pct < 10 for 2m -> create incident.
tess: Important constraint: never evict pinned embeddings below 10% cache occupancy. We lost a pinned key in a prior aggressive eviction run. Add a hard guard.
ciara: Filing incident ticket and attaching flamegraphs + allocation histograms. Link: https://redwood-internal/incident/2987654321
anya: Quick client-facing mitigation: short-circuit requests with seq > 4096 to return 413 SequenceTooLong and recommend client chunking. Implement as routing rule for affected routes.
matt: Thanks everyone. Schedule a 24h postmortem and draft an allocator tuning plan for next week. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: @matt created incident 2987654321 and scheduled postmortem 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC
kevin: Uploading perf profile (flamegraph + alloc histogram) to the ticket.
linh: Diagnostic probe snippet for the playbook:

curl -sS 'http://metrics.internal/gpu/probe?node=prod-17' | jq '.headroom, .kernel_path, .kv_hotset'

Use that to quickly check headroom and kernel choice before applying fixes.
ciara: Action items added to the incident: short-term config patches, RFC for persistent changes, alert rule, cautious KV eviction guard, client-side short-circuit rule.
anya: Closing thread. Monitoring channel for any return of the spike.
